ai.description: The Nilgiri frog (Dicroglossidae) reaches 3–4 cm. It is brown with dark dorsal mottling and a distinct light vertebral stripe. Key features include a pointed snout and prominent, interrupted skin ridges.
ai.identificationRemarks: The *Minervarya nilagirica* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous, and prominent glandular fold running along the sides of its back (dorsolateral fold).
ai.habitat: The Nilgiri frog inhabits evergreen forests and high-altitude grasslands in the Western Ghats, typically found near streams at elevations between 800 and 2,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Nilgiri frog is primarily nocturnal, remaining active during the night to forage for small insects among the leaf litter of forest floors and near water bodies.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Minervarya nilagirica* breeds during the monsoon, laying clutches of 100–300 eggs in shallow water or muddy depressions. Development follows a typical aquatic larval stage.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Minervarya nilagirica* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily occurring in the Nilgiri Hills across Kerala and Tamil Nadu at high elevations.
ai.callDescription: The Nilgiri Frog produces a series of rapid, high-pitched metallic "tink-tink" notes, typically heard from vegetation near forest streams and marshy habitats.
